intended_object: The canonical linear map over A = colim A_i, (colim M_i) ⊗_A (colim N_i) → colim_i (M_i ⊗_{A_i} N_i), for directed systems of modules M_i and N_i over a directed system of commutative semirings A_i. It sends [m_i] ⊗ [n_i] to [m_i ⊗ n_i]. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and the later use as the forward map of `tensorProductEquiv`.
explanation:
The definition is `TensorProduct.lift` applied to `pairingLinear`. That pairing is built from `DirectLimit.lift₂` applied to the stagewise maps (m, n) ↦ [i, m ⊗ n]. These maps are compatible with the transition maps, and the file proves that the pairing is bilinear over the limit semiring. By the universal property of the tensor product, this gives the canonical comparison map, with values on elementary tensors confirmed by `toTensorLimit_tmul_mk_mk`. The file then proves it is a bijection, with inverse `fromTensorLimit`, so it really is the standard isomorphism showing that tensor products commute with filtered colimits when the scalars vary.

The generality is natural: a directed nonempty preorder, commutative semirings, additive commutative monoids as modules, semilinear transition maps, and no injectivity assumed. Nonemptiness of ι is the usual requirement for the semiring structure on the concrete direct limit.

Mathlib only has the fixed-scalar version, for example `TensorProduct.directLimitLeft` for `Module.DirectLimit` over a single ring. I found nothing in Mathlib for varying scalar semirings, so the definition does not duplicate an existing more general construction.
